findings.source_quote: I brushed shoulders with well-known authors such as Katrina Hoover Lee, Johnny Miller, and Ruthann Stelfox.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the literal phrasing with a natural Hebrew equivalent meaning “I met / had the chance to meet well-known authors,” while keeping the names unchanged.
findings.translation_quote: נגעתי בכתפיהם של מחברים ידועים כגון Katrina Hoover Lee, Johnny Miller ו-Ruthann Stelfox.

findings.source_quote: I had the opportunity to sit under hours of inspirational and educational workshops
findings.suggested_fix: Use a natural Hebrew expression meaning that the writer attended hours of inspirational and educational workshops.
findings.translation_quote: הייתה לי ההזדמנות לשבת תחת שעות של סדנאות מעוררות השראה וחינוכיות

findings.source_quote: Fathers who with a concerned eye watch the world pressing in on the Christian homes.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace בתי־נוצרי with a grammatical Hebrew phrase meaning “Christian homes,” and preserve the source’s meaning that the world is pressing in on those homes.
findings.translation_quote: לאבות שמתבוננים בדאגה בעולמנו הלוחץ על בתי־נוצרי.

findings.source_quote: Nelson Mandela, former president of South Africa wrote, “Failure is a teacher, and at the end of your life, what do you think you’ll feel worst about, failing or never trying?”
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the entire quotation into Hebrew, preserving its question and meaning; for example: “כישלון הוא מורה, ובסוף חייך, מה לדעתך תצטער עליו יותר — שנכשלת או שמעולם לא ניסית?”
findings.translation_quote: נלסון מנדלה, נשיא דרום־אפריקה לשעבר, כתב: “Failure is a teacher, and at the end of your life, what do you think you’ll feel worst about, failing or never trying?”

findings.source_quote: This monumental event upended the vaccine debate
findings.suggested_fix: Replace התהפך על דיון החיסונים with a natural Hebrew expression conveying that the event overturned or radically changed the vaccine debate.
findings.translation_quote: אירוע ענק זה התהפך על דיון החיסונים
